g.text: Same mechanism as the paper's section 4.2 experiment (there: 0.8 s for a move followed by another move, 1 s otherwise). The

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: gain only appears when AGVs are faster than planned; when everyone is exactly on time both graphs give the same makespan.

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Planned waits vs emergent waits when AGVs run

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: L and X are lightly loaded and need only 0.5 s per move; everything else takes 1 s, a wait action also 1 s. With

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: waits in the graph, M and N still sit out their full planned waits. Without them, M and N wait exactly as long as

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: the dependencies require, and the gain cascades down the convoy.

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: M2 starts at 2.5 s: X left W13 at 2 s, but M's 1-s wait M1 must run out first

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: M2 starts at 2 s, the moment X2 completes
